title: HateCOT: An Explanation-Enhanced Dataset for Generalizable Offensive Speech Detection via Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper measured the ability of large language models to detect hate speech. Hate speech was defined based on attacks against individuals or groups due to protected characteristics, which explicitly includes 'religious affiliation' or 'religion'. The evaluation was not specific to religious hate speech but encompassed it within a broader definition.
findings: The paper does not provide findings specifically about religion. The general findings indicate that pretraining models on the HateCOT dataset improves their performance and data efficiency in detecting hate speech across various benchmarks. As these benchmarks define hate speech to include attacks based on religious affiliation, the improved performance implicitly covers the detection of anti-religious hate speech, but this category was not analyzed in isolation.
